SMTO-HTTP-0080 — The service kept redirecting SMTO, so it stopped

GUID: 2aecce26-24eb-492a-add5-0b6222e1bd65
Slug: http-redirect-limit
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service sent SMTO from one address to another more than five times. SMTO stopped following them so it wouldn't go around in circles.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to list the addresses the service sent it through. If the same addresses repeat, the service is stuck in a loop; if not, the last one is likely the right address.
  2. If the last address is the right one, use it directly: change Base URL for the connection in Parameter Store, or tell SMTO to use that address. Going straight to the final address avoids the chain of redirects.
  3. If the request was meant to change something, check in the service whether that change already happened before asking SMTO to try again. The service may have acted on the first request before it started redirecting.

What success looks like

  • The request reaches the service and returns a reply without hitting the redirect limit.

If it still fails

  • If the addresses go in a circle, the service itself likely has a problem. Send the copied error details to the person who runs it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP client stopped because following another redirect would exceed the maximum of five redirects.

What this means

  • Following another redirect would exceed the maximum of five already followed redirects. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Following another redirect would exceed the maximum of five already followed redirects.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained redirect chain for a loop or incorrect entry endpoint; earlier requests already reached their servers.

How to fix it

  • The client already followed MAX_REDIRECTS (5) in gateway_core/http_client.py. Inspect the redirects list in the receipt for a loop or a wrong base path, and send the request to the final intended URL; a loop back to a login page usually means the session or base_url is wrong.
  • Inspect the redirect chain for a loop or wrong endpoint and use the intended final endpoint.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A corrected intended endpoint finishes within the five-redirect bound.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
